note: One entry per clip. 'segments' is the narration: one line per on-screen caption, in the order the captions appear in the scene.

segments.caption: A decoder writes text one token at a time, from left to right.
segments.text: A decoder, like the one in G P T, writes text one token at a time from left to right. Here the note so far reads: the patient denies chest.

segments.caption: It predicts a probability for every token in the vocabulary.
segments.text: Given everything written so far, the decoder outputs a probability for every token in its vocabulary. The numbers on screen are illustrative.

segments.caption: Greedy decoding picks the most likely token: “pain”.
segments.text: Greedy decoding simply takes the most likely token, so the model writes pain, with a probability of zero point six two.

segments.caption: The new token is appended, and the model runs again.
segments.text: The chosen token is appended to the input, and the whole model runs again on the longer sequence to predict the next position.

segments.caption: Each forward pass adds one token: first “and”, then “dyspnea”.
segments.text: Each forward pass adds exactly one token. The second step adds and, and the third step adds dyspnea, meaning shortness of breath.

segments.caption: Greedy takes the top token; sampling draws by probability; temperature sets how random.
segments.text: Greedy decoding always takes the top token. Sampling draws a token according to the probabilities, and the temperature controls how random that draw is: low is nearly greedy, high is more varied.

segments.caption: Attention scores for five tokens: one row per query, one column per key.
segments.text: Here are the attention scores for five tokens: the patient denies chest pain. Each row is one token's query, and each column is a key.

segments.caption: “patient” must not see the words that come after it.
segments.text: But a decoder is trained to predict the next token. If patient could look at denies, chest, and pain, it would simply copy the answer.

segments.caption: The causal mask sets every score above the diagonal to minus infinity.
segments.text: The causal mask fixes this. Every score above the diagonal, where a query would look at a later token, is set to minus infinity.

segments.caption: After softmax, each row sums to 1 over allowed tokens; masked cells get 0.
segments.text: After the softmax, minus infinity becomes zero. Each row now sums to one over the tokens it is allowed to see: itself and the tokens before it.

segments.caption: “chest” attends only to The, patient, denies, and itself.
segments.text: For example, the row for chest spreads its attention over the, patient, denies, and chest itself, and gives nothing to pain.

segments.caption: One forward pass trains every position to predict its next token.
segments.text: Because of the mask, a single forward pass trains every position at once: each token's output is used to predict the token that follows it.

segments.caption: A vision transformer reads an image as a sequence of patches.
segments.text: A vision transformer, or V i T, uses the same encoder as a language model. It simply reads an image as a sequence of patches.

segments.caption: Cut the pathology tile into a 4 × 4 grid of patches.
segments.text: Here is a pathology tile stained with H and E: pink tissue and purple nuclei. We cut it into a four by four grid of patches.

segments.caption: The 16 patches line up into a sequence of 16 tokens.
segments.text: The sixteen patches are lined up in reading order, from top left to bottom right. Each patch now plays the role of a word token.

segments.caption: A linear projection turns each patch into a d-dimensional vector.
segments.text: Each patch is flattened into a list of pixel values, and a shared linear projection maps it to a vector with d dimensions.

segments.caption: A position vector tells the model where each patch came from.
segments.text: A position vector is added to each patch vector. Without it, the model would not know where in the image a patch came from.

segments.caption: A learnable [CLS] token is added at the front of the sequence.
segments.text: A learnable C L S token is placed at the front of the sequence. Its output will summarize the whole image.

segments.caption: The sequence of 17 tokens enters a standard transformer encoder.
segments.text: These seventeen tokens enter a standard transformer encoder. Nothing in the encoder is specific to images: it is the same architecture used for text.

segments.caption: The [CLS] output feeds a prediction head: tumor or normal.
segments.text: The output at the C L S position goes to a small prediction head, which classifies the tile as tumor or normal.

segments.caption: A 224 × 224 image with 16 × 16 patches gives 196 tokens.
segments.text: In practice, a two hundred twenty-four by two hundred twenty-four image with sixteen by sixteen pixel patches gives a fourteen by fourteen grid: one hundred ninety-six tokens.
